verses.text: These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul son of Kish. They were among the warriors who helped David in battle.
They were armed with bows and could shoot arrows or sling stones with either their right or left hand. They were relatives of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.
Their chief was Ahiezer, and then Joash, both sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. There were also Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu from Anathoth;
Ishmaiah from Gibeon, a mighty warrior among the Thirty and a leader of the Thirty; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad from Gederah;
Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite;
the Korahites Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam;
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

Some men from the tribe of Gad joined David at his fortress in the desert. They were brave warriors, trained for battle, who could use shield and spear. Their faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as fast as gazelles on the mountains.
Ezer was the chief, Obadiah was second, Eliab third,
Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,
Jeremiah tenth, and Machbannai eleventh.
These men from Gad were army commanders. The weakest of them could take on a hundred men, and the strongest a thousand.
They crossed the Jordan River in the first month of the year, when it was flooding all its banks. They chased away everyone living in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Some men from Benjamin and Judah also came to David at his fortress.

David went out to meet them and said, "If you have come in peace to help me, I am ready to join with you. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, even though I have done nothing wrong, may the God of our ancestors see it and punish you."

Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and he said, "We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, because your God helps you." So David welcomed them and made them leaders of his troops.

Some men from Manasseh also joined David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But David and his men did not help the Philistines. After talking it over, the Philistine rulers sent him away. They said, "It will cost us our heads if he goes back to his master Saul."
When David went to Ziklag, these men from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai. Each was a commander of a thousand in Manasseh.
They helped David fight against the raiding bands, because they were all brave warriors and commanders in his army.
Day after day men came to help David, until he had a great army, like the army of God.
These are the numbers of armed soldiers who came to David at Hebron to hand Saul's kingdom over to him, just as the LORD had said.
From Judah came six thousand eight hundred men armed for war, carrying shields and spears.
From Simeon came seven thousand one hundred brave warriors ready for battle.
From Levi came four thousand six hundred men.
Jehoiada, the leader of Aaron's family, came with three thousand seven hundred men,
and Zadok, a brave young warrior, came with twenty-two commanders from his family.
From Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, came three thousand men. Until then, most of them had stayed loyal to Saul's family.
From Ephraim came twenty thousand eight hundred brave warriors, famous in their own clans.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh came eighteen thousand men, chosen by name to come and make David king.
From Issachar came two hundred leaders who understood the times and knew what Israel should do. All their relatives followed their orders.
From Zebulun came fifty thousand experienced soldiers, ready for battle with every kind of weapon. They were completely loyal and ready to help David.
From Naphtali came one thousand commanders, with thirty-seven thousand men carrying shields and spears.
From Dan came twenty-eight thousand six hundred men ready for battle.
From Asher came forty thousand experienced soldiers ready for battle.
From the east side of the Jordan River, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, came one hundred and twenty thousand men armed with every kind of weapon.
All these were warriors who could take their places in battle. They came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. All the rest of the Israelites also agreed to make David king.
They stayed there with David for three days, eating and drinking, because their relatives had provided food for them.

Also, their neighbours from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. There were plenty of supplies: flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, olive oil, cattle, and sheep. There was great joy in Israel.
